what: EcoShift /api/liveconditions run on 16 Nov 2026 (burned ground from the Sentinel-2 burn ratio change, plus the other near-real-time checks)

warnings.text: Poor air (fine dust PM2.5 102.2 µg/m³, Copernicus CAMS): limit long hard work outdoors.

Likely burned ground, about 16.2 acres, in the south-east part of Farmland near Patiala: between 2026-10-28 and 2026-11-14 Sentinel-2 saw the burn ratio drop sharply and the ground turn dark like charred residue. Burning crop residue sends most of its nitrogen and sulfur into the air and burns off organic matter, so the soil there is less fertile and bare to wind and water erosion. If it was burned: plan extra nitrogen, test the soil, and next time leave or work in the residue. Check it on the ground first (fresh tillage or dark wet soil can look alike).

Farmland near Patiala was 98% bare soil on 2026-11-14. Bare soil over winter loses topsoil to wind and water; a cover crop or leaving residue protects it.
Farmland near Patiala: topsoil pH about 8 (alkaline, likely limy). Soybeans on high-pH soils can get iron deficiency chlorosis (yellow leaves): choose a tolerant variety.
Farmland near Patiala: low organic matter (about 9.6 g of carbon per kg of topsoil). Cover crops and leaving residue build it up and help the soil hold water.
